title: A personal needs assessment
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: If your education made you very specialized, what do you do about it now?

I said to a student: just as an exercise, I'm assuming, you were given the courses you needed in four years, and off you go, a graphic designer. In the real world you may say: I'm so specialized that I fit a corporate mould in a cubicle. What if I don't want that?
A student said: if you are already at that point, you have to continue your education, not necessarily going back to school, but continue learning and diversifying yourself.
I said we have doctors who study one organ. Everyone told us: focus, focus, get more specialized. I said a specialist who did not study habits may not tell you about your habits.

I asked a student who is a coach what advice they give. The student said: use the mastermind principle, with people around you who are better or smarter in certain areas. I also read, research online, and have a plan of how to progress.

How do you come up with that plan? I asked. The student said: have a focus. If you find a deficit in one area, read a few books, try a few things to implement the new ideas, test them, and keep adjusting.
I said: so you do a personal needs assessment. You diagnose the areas you want to work on, and then you build the curriculum around those areas.
The student described a progression from unconscious competence, to some competence, to confidence, even to a courageous level of understanding.
What is the deficit you will diagnose first?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write where your education left a gap.
Write the three areas you want to improve.
Write who could be in your mastermind.
Write a book or experiment for each area.
Write how you will test and adjust.

check.q: What did a student say to do if you are already specialized?
What did I call the student's method of diagnosing deficits?
What did the student say the mastermind principle is?
choices: Having people around you who are better or smarter in certain areas

recap: Diagnose your own gaps. Build your curriculum around them.
